name: security-azure-eventgrid-endpoint-binding-review
intent: Event Grid subscription validation and event-consumer authority
artifacts: Subscription creation, validation handshake, delivery authentication and webhook handler actions.
trace: Separate proof of endpoint control from proof that delivered events originate from the intended topic/tenant. Trace fields used for privileged downstream actions.
experiment: Use owned endpoints and synthetic events; compare a valid subscription/delivery with a locally forged event bearing the same data fields.
disproof: Echoing a validation code or accepting a public webhook request is not a protected effect by itself.
repair: Authenticate delivery context and constrain action resources, preserving legitimate subscription validation and retries.
branch_decisions: Endpoint validation establishes subscription delivery control; it does not make arbitrary future request bodies authentic. Identify the delivery schema and configured authentication mode, then trace verified subscription/source context into the consumer. A replayed legitimate event may be an idempotency issue, while an unsigned external body accepted as privileged input is a separate trust boundary.
operational_method: For Event Grid event schema, identify the POST Microsoft.EventGrid.SubscriptionValidationEvent and its data.validationCode; the synchronous ownership response echoes that value as validationResponse. CloudEvents v1.0 instead uses the OPTIONS abuse-protection handshake with WebHook-Request-Origin and WebHook-Allowed-Origin; it does not use the Event Grid validation-event mechanism. Retain configured delivery authentication separately from this endpoint-control handshake. Compare the correct schema handshake and one mismatched mode, then inspect an authentic synthetic business event versus an untrusted body at the protected consumer; echoing a validation code is not event authenticity.
